speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a low-grade fever, itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics; can you tell me the specific name of the antibiotic and how many days you took it? Also, when did these symptoms start appearing?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-Induced Maculopapular Eruption (Drug Eruption).

The clinical picture of a fever, itchy rash starting in flexural areas (antecubital/popliteal fossae), and joint pain appearing one week after starting amoxicillin is highly suggestive of a delayed hypersensitivity reaction to the antibiotic. Have you noticed any swelling of the lips, tongue, or face, or difficulty breathing?
